title: Dataset provenance manifest
description: Companion to each raw corpus. Required by project policy: training on data of unknown provenance is not acceptable, so license and source must be stated. Place next to the raw file as manifest.yaml or manifest.json; the pipeline reads it during `prepare` and warns loudly when a field is missing.

version.description: Version string. Bump on any content change.

source.description: Where the data came from. Be specific enough to re-acquire or audit.

license.description: SPDX identifier, or 'internal-use-only'. The value 'unknown' is treated as a provenance failure and reported in every run manifest.

content_hash.description: Content hash of the canonical serialised records. Set automatically by `prepare`; recorded in run manifests so a result can be tied to an exact dataset state.

categories.description: Task categories present, for coverage auditing.

annotation_method.description: How labels/answers were produced. State explicitly whether a human, an LLM, or a rule produced them. Never label model-generated text as human-annotated.
examples: reviewed by 2 agronomists, disagreements adjudicated by a third
synthesised by an LLM and NOT reviewed -- research only
extracted verbatim from published extension bulletins

known_limitations.description: Known bias or coverage gaps. Record them; do not hide them.
